text.p: Tropical Storm Fern is currently west of the Northern Marianas and is moving to the east at about 9 knots. Top winds have diminished to 45 knots and is expected to continue to weaken as it tracks to the east over the next 72 hours. The islands may still see some locally flooding rains and gusty winds from this storm and will continue to be somewhat of a risk to shipping routes.

Tropical cyclone Fergus continues to pack winds around 75 knots as it tracks to the south-southeast at a rapid 21 knots. Fergus is tracking just to the north of New Zealand and is expected to pass to the east of the North Island over the next 12-36 hours. The storm is expected to further weaken and become extra-tropical over the next 36 hours. Locally heavy rains and high winds will still be a problem in northern New Zealand while flash floodings are a risk. This storm should remain a major risk to shipping routes through the period.

Tropical cyclone Phil continues to track slowly off the northwest Australian coast. Still packing winds of 75 knots, this storm is expected to gradually turn west-southwest and slowly intensify over water. This storm will continue to spread flooding rains in the northwest through Monday. Main concern will be for shipping as it tracks off the coast and could significantly intensify.
